After the chunk a widget's `paint` receives its content-box size and its scene lands at the content-box origin inside the element's own transform (`M · T(content origin)`), so what it paints covers its content box exactly, with padding, border and a transform alike.

DioxusLabs/blitz issue #1578, read by `gh issue view 1578 -R DioxusLabs/blitz` on 2026-11-23 (state OPEN, 0 comments; body first 1500 characters):

Title: Custom widget paint receives border-box dimensions but is appended at a content-box origin in device axes

While integrating a Canvas custom widget on beta.4, the size passed to `Widget::paint` and the placement of the returned scene used different box/coordinate conventions. Both operations remain visible on the inspected main revision:

- [process_custom_widget_node](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/blitz/blob/beaa796f4ea698a738d7861aba81553563bfbc0b/packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs#L119) passes `final_layout().size * scale` (border-box dimensions).
- [draw_custom_widget](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/blitz/blob/beaa796f4ea698a738d7861aba81553563bfbc0b/packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs#L1399) appends at `content_box().origin()` using `self.transform.then_translate(...)` (translation after the element transform).

A minimal diagnostic setup is a `Widget` whose `paint` logs its width/height and returns an opaque rectangle from `(0,0)` to those supplied dimensions, attached to:

```html
<canvas style="box-sizing:content-box;width:100px;height:60px;
  padding:12px;border:3px solid black;
  transform-origin:0 0;transform:rotate(30deg) scale(1.4,.8)"></canvas>
```

At scale 1 the current callback size is 130 x 90, while the append origin is the content origin (15,15). A rectangle of that callback size starting there extends into/beyond the content box. Separately, the `(15,15)` offset is added in output axes, so it does not rotate/scale with the box. The expected placement for a content scene is `M * T(content_origin)`, not `T(content_origin) * M`.

title: I3-canvas-research-2026-11-18.md.txt
body:
# Headless canvas — what exists and what escher can take (the escher overseer's research, 2026-11-18)

Asked by the founder after 0.3.0 closed: «И по хорошему прежде чем стартовать надо ресерчнуть по поводу хедлесс
канваса как что где реализовано, и подумать что мы можем себе взять». Four read-only passes, returned by
2026-11-18 21:54Z: three over the web, one over escher's tree as it stood on disk after `bc7661240`. Each claim
is marked: **[P]** the agent fetched the primary page (through a summarizing fetch, so a quote is its extract),
**[S]** a search summary only, **[code]** read in escher's tree by a read-only agent (no build, no git).
Nothing here was built or run; every code fact is a hypothesis for the phase that touches it to re-measure.

## 1. escher's own ground (code facts; they correct `intent.md` findings 3–7)
- A `<canvas>` is `SpecialElementData::Canvas(CanvasData { custom_paint_source_id: u64 })`
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:372`, `:1012`); the id is parsed from `<canvas src="N">` and
  `canvas_data()` has no caller. `blitz-paint` names `Canvas` nowhere. [code]
- What paints today is the **`Widget` trait** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs:75`):
  `paint(&mut dyn RenderContext, styles, width, height, scale) -> Scene`, registered by
  `doc.mutate().set_custom_widget(node_id, Box<dyn Widget>)`; `blitz-paint` appends the widget's scene
  (`render.rs:615`, `:1377`) behind the `custom-widget` feature. Upstream replaced `CustomPaintSource` with it in
  blitz PR #425 [P]. The path is CPU-safe: a scene fragment, no GPU handle unless the widget downcasts for one.
- **The harness may paint no widget at all:** `packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml:18` takes `blitz-paint` with
  `default-features = false`, which drops `custom-widget`, unless another crate of the build unifies it. Not
  measurable by reading: the FIRST measurement of the version. [code]
- Headless shots: `render_to_buffer::<VelloCpuImageRenderer, _>` (`blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:83`);
  pins `anyrender 0.15.0`, `anyrender_vello_cpu 0.19.0`, `anyrender_serialize 0.9.0` (root `Cargo.toml:121-125`),
  the last used by `apps/browser` alone. [code]
- Reserved already: `Placer::App { canvas }` in the `layout` verb («Reserved: nothing places a node so yet»,
  `packages/escher-driver/src/layout.rs:58`); a commented `accessibility_tree` on `Widget` under «TODO: allow for
  multiple nodes per widget» (`custom_widget.rs:144`); `Harness::drag(from, to, steps)` with `mouse_down_at`,
  `move_mouse_to`, `mouse_up_at` (`blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:112-150`); `Widget::handle_event`. [code]
- Not there: a snapshot node needs an `author_id` AND a DOM element (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:153`),
  so no non-DOM node can appear; the graph reserves no id form for one; the driver has fifteen verbs, none `drag`
  (`command.rs:935,945` pin 15 and `(11, 3, 1)`); no stand app holds a canvas (two engine tests do). [code]
- An action's point is the centre of the snapshot bounds, checked by `visible_region` — «Exact under a translate
  and a scale; under a rotation it reads the bounding box» (`execute.rs:652`, `blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:816`). [code]

## 2. Painting headless on the CPU
- Upstream Blitz has no Canvas 2D context and expects the embedder to bring one (PR #1210, open) [P]; open issue
  #1578: a widget's paint gets the border-box size but is placed at the content-box origin [P].
- `anyrender_vello_cpu` paints `Paint::Custom` / `Paint::Resource` transparent with no warning, ignores backdrop
  filters, and drops layer filters when multithreaded [P] — the dead end is anything routed through a texture.
- **Servo is the one production Canvas2D on `vello_cpu`** (`components/canvas/vello_cpu_backend.rs`): clip stack,
  composite ops as blend layers, `clear_rect`, text as glyph runs. MPL-2.0, tied to Servo's crates — a mapping to
  read, not a crate to take; shadows unimplemented [P].
- Other rasterizers: tiny-skia has no text [P]; raqote and forma are stale [P]; skia-safe is a Skia dependency.
  No standalone native Canvas2D crate was found [S].
- Determinism: nobody claims bit-exact output across architectures. Vello's own tests compare with a tolerance
  [P]; @napi-rs/canvas documents one colour level of difference between x64 and arm64 and makes text portable only
  with registered fonts, full glyph coverage and a fixed language [P]. `vello_cpu` offers an `f32_pipeline`
  «useful for test snapshots» [P]; whether its output varies by SIMD level was not found.

## 3. The canvas read as data
- **Flutter's DisplayList test form is the closest precedent:** one line per op in paint order, layers as
  indentation, equality of two lists [P]. Skia's debugger adds the clip and matrix at each command and a filter by
  command name; `skp_parser` dumps JSON with images and typefaces by reference [P/S].
- WebRender derives its capture from the types through serde; its hand-kept YAML writer «was frequently broken» [P].
- jest-canvas-mock keeps two granularities: every call, and effective draws only [P].
- Excalidraw, tldraw and Konva assert on the object model, never on draw calls [S] — the dump should group by
  logical object.
- Not found anywhere: how large such dumps get, float rounding practice, a diff of two dumps. Ours to measure.

## 4. Virtual nodes, `drag`, pan and zoom
- **Flutter `CustomPainterSemantics`**: the painter returns a list of `{key, rect, properties, transform}` per
  paint [P]. Android's `ExploreByTouchHelper` is the callback form (`getVirtualViewAt`, populate, perform) with
  explicit invalidation, mandatory after an add or a remove [P]. Qt has `isValid()` for a stale object [P].
- **AccessKit carries nodes with no DOM behind them:** `bounds` in the node's space, a `transform` applied to the
  node and its descendants, `is_hidden`, `is_disabled`, `clips_children`; it has no drag action [P].
- The web removed `addHitRegion` because it altered hit testing (whatwg/html PR #1942) [P]; Figma mirrors its
  canvas into a DOM generated from an internal accessibility tree [S]; React Flow and tldraw keep nodes in the DOM
  and only edges or geometry in canvas [P].
- Drivers: Playwright `dragTo(target, {sourcePosition, targetPosition, steps})`, `steps` defaulting to 1, and its
  note that a manual drag needs at least two moves [P]; flutter_test splits a drag in two or the update never
  fires, and has `panZoomStart/Update/End` [P]; WebDriver wheel and pointer moves with `move target out of
  bounds` [P]; kittest drives by accessibility query plus `drag_at` / `drop_at` [P].

## 4a. Upstream's own status page (for 0.5.0's modern-HTML probe; fetched 2026-11-18 22:15Z, the founder's pointer)
`blitz.is/status/css`, `/status/elements`, `/status/events` and roadmap issue #119, read by a fetch agent [P]. It
describes UPSTREAM main, not escher: escher's own `<select>` reads «Not supported» there. Each line is the page's
word, to be measured on escher before it is relied on.
- `position: sticky` — In Progress (blitz#887; the roadmap puts it at 1.0). `fixed`, `absolute`, `z-index` — Supported.
- `scroll-snap-type` / `-align` / `-stop` — Not supported. `overflow: auto` — Not supported (`scroll`, `hidden`,
  `clip` are). `scroll-margin`, `scroll-padding`, `overscroll-behavior` — Not supported.
- Transitions and Animations — Supported. `clip-path`, `mask-*`, `box-shadow`, `opacity`, 2D `transform` —
  Supported (a node with opacity is clipped whatever its overflow). The roadmap still lists clip-path, mask and
  animations as pending: the two pages disagree.
- `filter` — Partial: «Supported with the Skia backend. Partially supported (blur and drop-shadow only) with Vello
  Hybrid.» `backdrop-filter` — Partial: «Supported with the Skia backend.» Neither names the CPU backend our
  headless shots use. `mix-blend-mode`, `background-blend-mode` — Not supported.
- 3D transforms, `perspective`, the individual `scale` / `rotate` / `translate` properties, `transform-box` — Not supported.
- SVG — Partial: static only, no CSS `fill` / `stroke`, no filters. `<canvas>` — «A proprietary API to render a raw
  WGPU texture is supported».
- Events: no drag events, no `ResizeObserver` / `IntersectionObserver` / `MutationObserver`, no `change`, `resize`,
  `load`. Elements: no `dialog`, `progress`, `meter`, `video`, `picture`.
- Subgrid, anchor positioning, multi-column, `content-visibility` — Not supported.

## 5. What the overseer proposes to take (a proposal for the route and its phases, not a decision)
1. **Paint through `Widget::paint -> Scene`, on the pinned `vello_cpu`.** No new rasterizer, no texture path.
   First entry: measure whether the harness paints a widget, and make the stand's canvas fixture show in a shot.
2. **No Canvas 2D context of our own in 0.4.0** unless the founder asks for one: the app paints with anyrender's
   scene API. Servo's backend is the reference if a 2D context is ever wanted.
3. **The read verb prints the recorded scene in Flutter's shape**, generated from `RenderCommand` by serde,
   heavy data by reference, glyph runs as their text, a summary level and a full level, filters by kind and
   region — grouped by virtual node where one covers the commands.
4. **Virtual nodes declared as a per-paint list** `{key, role, name, rect in canvas space, disabled}` beside the
   scene, emitted as AccessKit nodes under the canvas with the canvas's transform; the author key is the id
   (his KEYS + ANCHORS ruling of 2026-10-06); a key gone at action time is a `stale` refusal.
5. **Regions give semantics and refusals; events still go to the widget as ordinary pointer events at the
   resolved point** — the `addHitRegion` lesson.
6. **`drag <src> (to <dst> | by dx,dy)` with several interpolated moves by default**, source and destination
   both checked for refusals first, on the harness's existing primitive. Zoom is its own verb (wheel, pinch).
7. **Determinism stated honestly:** bundled fonts (v030-14), one thread, and a measurement on CI's hosts of
   whether a canvas shot is byte-equal across Linux, macOS and Windows; the data form is the primary observation
   and does not depend on it.

## Forks that look like the founder's (each at its phase, with its measurement)
- A Canvas 2D context (the web API, for page scripts) or anyrender's scene API alone.
- The declaration form: a per-paint list, or callbacks with invalidation.
- What the read verb may carry to a model provider (a boundary widening: authored text in glyph runs).
- Cross-host pixel equality of a canvas: required, or a stated tolerance.

## Sources
Blitz PR #425 · #225 · #1210 · issue #1578 (github.com/DioxusLabs/blitz) · anyrender `crates/anyrender_vello_cpu/src/scene.rs`
(github.com/DioxusLabs/anyrender) · Servo `components/canvas/vello_cpu_backend.rs` (github.com/servo/servo) ·
docs.rs/vello_cpu · github.com/Brooooooklyn/canvas · Flutter `display_list_testing.cc`
(flutter.googlesource.com/mirrors/engine) · skia.org/docs/dev/tools/debugger ·
kvark.github.io/webrender/debug/ron/2018/01/23/wr-capture-infra.html · github.com/hustcc/jest-canvas-mock ·
api.flutter.dev (`CustomPainterSemantics`, `WidgetController.drag`, `TestGesture`) ·
developer.android.com/reference/androidx/customview/widget/ExploreByTouchHelper · doc.qt.io/qt-6/qaccessibleinterface.html ·
docs.rs/accesskit (`Node`, `Action`, `NodeId`) · github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1942 ·
figma.com/blog/building-accessibility-into-a-canvas-based-product · reactflow.dev/learn/advanced-use/testing ·
tldraw.dev/docs/shapes · playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-drag-to · w3.org/TR/webdriver2 ·
docs.rs/kittest · docs.rs/egui_kittest

text in this chunk).

The forks file's option **A**: the document's own font context handed to the widget — a new defaulted method on

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text · **Version:** escher-0.4.0

A widget an app paints from Rust (architecture · established-decisions/decision/custom-widget-object) is placed at its
content box and draws its text from the document's own fonts, measured on the stand in both layout modes.

Three engine changes, each behind `custom-widget` and each the founder's ruling (`inputs#I5`, relayed verbatim through
the overseers; the operator resumed the phase on it, `inputs#I4`):

- **The paint at the content box (F1 option A, upstream issue #1578, `inputs#I2`).** Today `process_custom_widget_node`
  hands `Widget::paint` the border-box size and `draw_custom_widget` appends the scene at the content origin in output
  axes (`T(content origin) · M`). After the chunk `paint` is handed the content-box size × scale and the scene lands at
  `M · T(content origin)`, the form `draw_image` already uses. Measured at P3 (research §The stand measurement): a
  content-box `<object>` with `padding: 12px; border: 3px` is handed `(130, 90)` and paints red outside its border box;
  under `scale(2)` its scene starts at device x = 23 where `M · T` puts it at 38; a prototype reads `(100, 60)` and those
  pixels white. The scene stays unclipped (option B not taken).

- **The pointer events in the same frame (F1 option C).** The pointer events `handle_dom_event` forwards to a widget
  carry coordinates relative to its content-box origin — the border-box origin `absolute_position` reads plus its left
  and top border and padding, CSS px, untransformed as today — so a widget hears pointer coordinates in the frame it
  paints in. A sub-document's events are unmoved.

- **Canvas text from the document's fonts (F2 option A).** blitz-paint hands each widget the document's own font
  context before its `paint`, through a new defaulted `Widget` method, and `BaseDocument` gains a public accessor of its
  font context, both behind `custom-widget` — so canvas text is shaped from the very context the document's text is
  (v030-14's acceptance wording) and, on the stand, from the bundled DejaVu Sans (architecture ·
  standard-contracts/decision/stand-typography-dejavu-sans).

Each is a direct engine change for every document behind the feature, flagged upstreamable, nothing sent (architecture ·
established-decisions/decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable); each fork addition to an upstream function
goes into an escher function with one call in upstream's body (architecture ·
stack-and-technologies/decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions). Three new stand checks are the witnesses, each run red
first and its red reading kept (the operator's directive, `inputs#I1`; test-plan ·
unit-test-strategy/decision/mutation-controlled-tests). Canvas text leaves only as pixels in a shot, inside the
ratified crossing (security-plan · threat-model-summary/decision/canvas-content-crosses-as-shot-pixels); no verb,
argument, carrier, field, cause, session error, exit, log field or span is added.

1. **The placement check first, red** — create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_placement.rs` (keeps arch S1–S4,
   tests S1–S9, layouts S1–S2, design S2, obs S1–S3, security S1–S3, a11y S1–S2). It opens with a `//!` doc naming the
   behaviour (a widget is handed its content-box size and its scene lands at its content origin inside the element's
   transform, both layout modes) and the upstream defect it guards, `https://github.com/DioxusLabs/blitz/issues/1578`
   (arch S4, tests S2). It holds a private widget `ContentFill` filling `Rect(0, 0, width, height)` with
   `Color::from_rgb8(255, 0, 0)` as `stand_canvas_shot`'s `RedFill` does, and recording the `(width, height)` it was
   handed into a shared cell the test reads (an `Arc<Mutex<…>>` held by the test and the widget); each case boots one
   component through `stand::boot_alone(…, stand::options(incremental))` inside `Session::start("canvas", …)`, for
   `incremental` in `[false, true]`, and reads `session.harness_mut().screenshot()`. Three tests, every pixel a measured
   literal (research §The stand measurement, `evidence/p3-probe-{unfixed,fixed}.log`):
   - `a_padded_widget_paints_its_content_box` — `object` styled `display: block; box-sizing: content-box; width: 100px;
     height: 60px; padding: 12px; border: 3px solid black;`. Its fixture's condition first: the snapshot reads the
     object's bounds `(8.0, 8.0, 130.0, 90.0)`. Then the handed size reads `(100, 60)`; (50, 50) and (120, 80) read
     `[255, 0, 0, 255]`; (125, 50) (padding), (145, 50) and (50, 105) (outside the border box) read
     `[255, 255, 255, 255]`.
   - `a_transformed_widget_paints_inside_its_transform` — the same object plus `transform-origin: 0 0; transform:
     scale(2);`. Handed `(100, 60)`; (40, 40) and (236, 100) red; (26, 26), (34, 34), (245, 100) and (255, 100) white.
   - `a_widget_with_no_padding_paints_its_whole_box` — `display: block; width: 200px; height: 100px;`. Handed
     `(200, 100)`; (58, 58) and (207, 107) red; (209, 109) white (the row the fix must not move).
   Run gate 3 on the untouched engine: the first two tests red (handed `(130, 90)`; (145, 50) red), the third green.
   Copy the log to `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text/evidence/red-placement.log`, every
   host path respelled (security S3).

2. **The paint fix** — in `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs`, `process_custom_widget_node` takes the paint size from a
   new private escher function beside it, `content_box_paint_size`, which reads the node's `final_layout()` and returns
   its size less left/right (top/bottom) border and padding, floored at 0, × `scale`, as `u32` — one call in upstream's
   body replacing the two `final_layout().size` lines (the `width == 0 || height == 0` early return stays). In
   `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs`, `draw_custom_widget` composes the content-origin translation with
   `self.transform.pre_translate(Vec2 { x, y })` in place of `then_translate` (one line; no clip layer, option B not
   taken). Gate 3 reads 3 passed in both layout modes.

3. **The pointer-frame check first, red** — create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_pointer_frame.rs` (keeps the
   same standing lines as step 1; its `//!` names the behaviour and cites #1578 as the paint's companion). A private
   widget `PointerLog` paints nothing and records each `UiEvent::PointerDown` and `UiEvent::PointerMove` it hears in
   `handle_event` (`page_x`, `page_y`, `client_x`, `client_y`) into a shared cell. One test,
   `a_padded_widget_hears_pointer_events_from_its_content_box`, on the padded object of step 1 (no transform), both
   layout modes: `session.harness_mut().mouse_down_at(50.0, 50.0)` then `move_mouse_to(120.0, 80.0)`. Fixture's
   condition first: the widget heard exactly one `PointerDown` (the hit reached the object). Predicted (from
   `events/mod.rs:22-31` and `:135`, the harness setting page = client, test-plan ·
   3-test-harness-contract/contract/harness-input/pointer-coordinates): today `(42, 42)` and `(112, 72)` — the
   border-box origin (8, 8); after step 4 `(27, 27)` and `(97, 57)` — the content origin (23, 23); page and client
   alike. Record what the red run measures; the test pins the measured literals. A measured value off the prediction
   stops the step and is reported, never pinned. Run gate 4 red and keep
   `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text/evidence/red-pointer-frame.log`.

4. **The pointer-frame fix** — in `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`, the `custom-widget` arm of
   `handle_dom_event` passes `map_dom_event_to_ui_event` the offset a new private escher function returns,
   `custom_widget_content_origin`, gated `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")]`: `pos` plus the node's `final_layout()`
   `border.left + padding.left` and `border.top + padding.top` — one call in upstream's body; `pos` and the
   sub-document arm untouched. Gate 4 reads 1 passed.

5. **The font-context surface, no call yet** — in `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs` the `Widget` trait
   gains a defaulted method `fonts(&mut self, fonts: &Arc<Mutex<parley::FontContext>>)` (the default ignores it), its
   `///` saying it is handed the document's own font context before each `paint`, so text the widget draws is shaped
   from the fonts the document's text is (arch S5); in `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, `BaseDocument` gains
   `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")] pub fn font_ctx(&self) -> Arc<Mutex<parley::FontContext>>` returning a clone of
   its `font_ctx`, with a `///` naming it as the context a custom widget shapes its text from — the prototype's form
   (`evidence/p3-probe-prototypes.diff.txt`). No implementor changes (the method is defaulted): the sweep of research
   §Sweeps (`RedFill`, both `DemoWidget`s, `FpsWidget`) is re-read and each left as it is.

6. **The text check first, red** — `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]` gains
   `parley = { workspace = true }` (architecture · conventions/decision/workspace-dependencies), and the lock's
   `blitz-tests` entry its one `"parley"` line, written by one resolution with no `--locked` —
   `cargo tree --offline -p blitz-tests --depth 0` — read by gate 9 as one added line; every later cargo run passes
   `--locked`. Create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_text.rs` (keeps step 1's standing lines and design S1). Two
   private widgets draw «Hg» at 40 px in black at the same origin from `parley`-shaped glyph runs into their `Scene`, as
   the P3 probe did (`evidence/p3-probe.rs.txt`): `DocumentText` shapes from the context its `fonts` method was handed
   (nothing handed → it draws nothing) and keeps that `Arc` for the test; `BundledText` shapes from its own
   `blitz_dom::build_single_font_ctx(seven_guis::DEJAVU_SANS)`. One test,
   `canvas_text_is_shaped_from_the_documents_own_fonts`, both layout modes, each widget on a
   `display: block; width: 200px; height: 100px;` object booted as step 1 boots: the fixture's condition first — the
   context `DocumentText` was handed is the document's own (`Arc::ptr_eq` with the harness document's `font_ctx()`);
   then the 200 × 100 region of its shot holds at least one dark pixel (every channel ≤ 128) and equals, byte for
   byte, the same region of `BundledText`'s shot — the canvas text is the bundled DejaVu Sans the document's text is
   (P3 measured the two routes byte-equal on the stand, `equal_to_route_b=true`, `evidence/p3-probe-route-a.log`).
   A whole-region comparison between two widgets on one host, never a pixel count, so no host's rasterization is
   pinned (test-plan · 2-test-strategy/decision/cross-os-checks-hold-no-shot). Run gate 5 on the tree as step 5 leaves
   it (no hand-off call): red, the handed context absent. Keep
   `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text/evidence/red-text.log`.

7. **The hand-off** — in `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs`, `process_custom_widget_node` reads the document's
   `font_ctx()` before it borrows the node and calls `widget_data.widget.fonts(&…)` immediately before `paint` (one
   added call; the prototype's two lines). Gates 5 and 6 read 1 passed — gate 6 under
   `--features blitz-paint/font-embolden`, whose engine embolden the widget's own glyph runs bypass; if gate 6 reads
   red there, the step stops and reports it (the founder was shown the bypass at F2).

8. **The controls** — after gates 1–8 read green, /implement makes ONE one-shot `gate.py control` run, never an entry
   (gate-contract.md §Control), its controls file in the run dir, four controls, each `case` its guard's own test:
   - `paint-size` · entry 3 · the `content_box_paint_size` call in `process_custom_widget_node` replaced by upstream's
     border-box reading (the `old` the call line as written, the `new` the two `final_layout().size` lines) · case
     `a_padded_widget_paints_its_content_box`;
   - `paint-origin` · entry 3 · `render.rs` `self.transform.pre_translate(Vec2 { x, y })` → `self.transform.then_translate(Vec2 { x, y })`
     · case `a_transformed_widget_paints_inside_its_transform`;
   - `pointer-frame` · entry 4 · the `custom_widget_content_origin(…)` argument in the widget arm replaced by `pos` ·
     case `a_padded_widget_hears_pointer_events_from_its_content_box`;
   - `font-handoff` · entry 5 · the `widget_data.widget.fonts(…)` line removed · case
     `canvas_text_is_shaped_from_the_documents_own_fonts`.
   Each entry carries `--no-fail-fast`, so every case is reached. Kill `--timeout 1200` (a per-package rebuild of
   blitz-dom or blitz-paint and their dependents plus one target); a `timeout` reading is not read as held — that
   control is re-fired once, then stopped on. The four `holds` lines are recorded beside the red readings of steps 1, 3
   and 6.
9. **The wider gates** — gates 7–13 in order.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_placement.rs` — the placement check (F1 A), three tests, both layout modes
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_pointer_frame.rs` — the pointer-frame check (F1 C), both layout modes
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_text.rs` — the canvas-text check (F2 A), both layout modes
- `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs` — `content_box_paint_size` (step 2) and the font hand-off before `paint` (step 7)
- `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` — `draw_custom_widget` appends at `M · T(content origin)` (step 2)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs` — `custom_widget_content_origin` in the widget arm (step 4)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs` — the defaulted `Widget::fonts` (step 5)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the public `BaseDocument::font_ctx()` behind `custom-widget` (step 5)
- `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` — `parley = { workspace = true }` as a dev-dependency (step 6)
- `Cargo.lock` — the `blitz-tests` entry gains `parley`; no package added (step 6)
**The gates:**
- blitz-dom's and blitz-paint's own unit tests, the custom-widget replay test among them (gates 1, 2);

- the three new checks per package, each read red before its fix (gates 3–5), and the text check under
  `blitz-paint/font-embolden` (gate 6, the local witness of a paint change under that feature);

- the two standing widget readers, `stand_canvas_shot` and `custom_widget_layout`, which the fix must leave green
  (gate 7), then the whole of blitz-tests per package (gate 8);
- the lock probe: one line added, none removed (gate 9; no line on the untouched tree);

- the pre-push gate `fast` (workspace tests, both clippy lines — blitz-dom's `--no-default-features … custom-widget`
  line among them — and `embolden`), the `doc` leg (two new public doc comments; test-plan ·
  9-ci-integration/decision/doc-leg-gates-public-doc-edits), the `audit` leg (the lock moves; security-plan ·
  dependency-security/decision/local-audit-before-push) and `stand-repeat`, which takes the three `stand_` checks by
  their prefix (gates 10–13).

**What no step changes:** no boot path or binary start (no served task holds a widget; the stand's boots are
untouched), so no smoke entry; no log site, span or field; no served task, kept check or committed check, so `host_log`,
`mcp_log`, `stand_cross_os_readings`' table and the cold-agent pipe move nothing (all read inside `fast` and
`stand-repeat`); no a11y leg file. There is no live leg and no headful self-verify on this project.

**Controls.** Each new check is red before its fix (steps 1, 3, 6) and under step 8's one-shot `gate.py control`; gate 9
reads no line on the untouched tree. No other new control.

The diff is not OS-sensitive: no OS `cfg` site is added (the added `cfg`s are the `custom-widget` feature's). The text
check compares two widgets on one host and pins no rasterized pixel, so CI's macOS and Windows test legs read it as
Linux does. The operator's hygiene, push and CI entries stand because this chunk's verdict reads a CI run.

- Upstreamable, flagged and not sent: the paint placement (#1578), the widget pointer frame, the `Widget::fonts` method
  and `BaseDocument::font_ctx()` — named in the wrap's handoff.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** (authority for each engine change: the founder, 2026-11-23, relayed verbatim through

  - architecture §Established Decisions — `+` a decision beside `(architecture ·

  - architecture §Standard Contracts — `~ (architecture · standard-contracts/contract/nodes-widgets/widget-trait)` or a
    `+` contract beside it: the defaulted `Widget::fonts` hands the document's own font context before each paint; `+`
    a `BaseDocument · font_ctx` contract (public, behind `custom-widget`, the document's shared font context); ratified.
  - security-plan §Input Validation — `+` a decision beside `(security-plan ·
    input-validation/decision/custom-widget-initial-attribute-replay)`: behind `custom-widget` a widget's paint size,

  - security-plan §Dependency Security — `+` or `~` the reviewed pinning fact: blitz-tests takes `parley` as a
    dev-dependency, the workspace's one registry version, one lock line, no package, the audit green with `deny.toml`

  - test-plan §2 Test Strategy — `+` the three checks as the witnesses of the widget's content-box paint, pointer frame

record.title: A canvas painted headless
record.requirement: What an app paints into a canvas from Rust appears in a headless screenshot, its text from the bundled fonts, its cross-host byte equality measured and required or given a tolerance by the founder's word; Circle Drawer moves onto a real canvas
record.observed_gap: An app paints through the widget trait, appended behind a feature the headless harness drops unless another crate unifies it, so whether a headless shot paints a widget at all is unmeasured; the CPU backend paints custom and resource paints transparent with no warning; a widget's paint gets the border-box size placed at the content-box origin (upstream #1578); no stand app holds a canvas, Circle Drawer's canvas being an ordinary element.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, a shot of Circle Drawer shows the circles its app painted from Rust and canvas text drawn from the bundled fonts, in both layout modes; the canvas shot's bytes are measured on CI's Linux, macOS and Windows hosts and held equal or within the tolerance the founder set.

record.notes:
2026-11-23 (2026-11-23-canvas-in-a-headless-shot, phase P5): not claimed — a widget painted from Rust on an `<object data>` is planned to show in a harness and a driver shot in every build selection, on the stand in process (stand_canvas_shot); the acceptance's Circle Drawer, canvas text and cross-host legs stay with «Canvas placement and text», «Canvas shot across hosts» and «Circle Drawer on a canvas».

2026-11-23 (2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text, phase P5): not claimed — a widget's paint placed at its content box inside its element's transform (upstream #1578), its pointer events in the same content-box frame, and canvas text shaped from the document's own font context are planned on the stand in process (stand_canvas_placement, stand_canvas_pointer_frame, stand_canvas_text), on the founder's F1 A+C and F2 A; the acceptance's Circle Drawer and cross-host legs stay with «Canvas shot across hosts» and «Circle Drawer on a canvas».

body:
**Chunk:** a widget painted at its content box (upstream #1578) and canvas text from the bundled fonts
**Date:** 2026-11-23
**Run:** 2026-11-23T10-01-43-implement

- **Files:** `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs` · `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` · `Cargo.lock` · new: `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_placement.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_pointer_frame.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_text.rs`

title: evidence/founder-forks.md
body:
# Founder forks — 2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text («Canvas placement and text», v040-09)

Written at P3 of the take-up (run `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T08-25-01-phase/`), on the operator's directive
(`inputs#I1`): every fork that is the operator's — a boundary widening, a new carrier, verb, crossing or public
surface, a bundled font or asset entering the tree, a choice that turns what the canvas is — is written here and
answered by no default. Two forks stand (F1, F2); one candidate is settled by a standing record and named at the
end. Every path below is project-relative; the probe's logs in this folder are respelled (no temp or home path).

## What was measured first, on the stand (the ground both forks stand on)

A throwaway probe in a detached worktree of HEAD `d43bc0e7f`, never committed (`p3-probe.rs.txt`), booted through
`seven_guis::stand::boot_alone` at the stand's options, both layout modes, read by `Harness::screenshot`. An
`<object>` carries a `CustomWidgetAttr` of a widget that fills `(0, 0, width, height)` red and records the size it
was handed. Logs: `p3-probe-unfixed.log` (HEAD), `p3-probe-route-a.log` (HEAD + the route-A prototype),
`p3-probe-fixed.log` (HEAD + route A + the placement-fix prototype); the prototypes' diff:
`p3-probe-prototypes.diff.txt`.

| Case (body margin 8) | HEAD — the red reading | With the placement-fix prototype |
|---|---|---|
| `box-sizing: content-box; width: 100px; height: 60px; padding: 12px; border: 3px solid` — border box (8,8)–(138,98), content box (23,23)–(123,83) | `paint` handed `(130, 90)`, the border box; red at (125,50) in the padding and at (145,50) and (50,105), **outside the element** | handed `(100, 60)`; (50,50), (120,80) red; (125,50), (130,50), (145,50), (50,90), (50,105) white |
| the same with `transform-origin: 0 0; transform: scale(2)` — `M · T(content origin)` puts the scene at device x = 38; today's `T(content origin) · M` at 23 | handed `(130, 90)`; red at (26,26), (34,34), (255,100) | handed `(100, 60)`; (26,26), (34,34), (245,100), (255,100) white; (40,40), (236,100) red |
| `width: 200px; height: 100px`, no padding or border (the shape `stand_canvas_shot` holds) | handed `(200, 100)`; red inside, white outside | unchanged |

Both layout modes read alike in every row. With the fix prototype the standing checks `stand_canvas_shot` (2
tests) and `custom_widget_layout` (6) read green. Canvas text: a widget shaping «Hg» at 40 px sans-serif through
parley and drawing its glyph runs reads 557 dark pixels in its 200 × 100 canvas, both layout modes byte-equal, on
either F2 route — and the two routes' frames are byte-equal on the stand.

**Facts both forks depend on.** No served task holds a widget today (the previous chunk's measurement). The
`custom-widget` feature is compiled into the harness, the driver and `escher-session` in every build selection
(architecture `decision/harness-paints-custom-widgets`) and into the browser and any dioxus-native app whose
features unify it; a widget is reached only by app code in Rust (`CustomWidgetAttr` on an `<object>`), never by
page markup.

---

## Fork F1 — the widget placed at its content box (upstream #1578): an engine change, and how far it reaches

**What crosses.** Nothing crosses a carrier: no verb, field, cause, exit, log field or span moves, and a shot's
fields are unmoved. What changes is the engine's behaviour for **every document that holds a custom widget**, in
every app that builds `custom-widget` (the stand, the driver and `escher-session`, the browser, any dioxus-native
app): the size a widget's `paint` is handed and where its scene lands. A widget with no padding, border or
transform reads the same as today (measured, row 3).

**The rule of ours it meets.**
- An engine change for every document is ratified per change: the nearest precedent, behind this same feature, is
  security-plan `decision/custom-widget-initial-attribute-replay` («an engine change for every document behind the
  feature, ratified»); the session learning of 2026-10-18 makes a fork whose options each change engine behaviour
  for every document, with no ruling behind it, the founder's.
- Architecture `decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable`: the fix is flagged upstreamable and nothing
  is sent; upstream issue #1578 is open (`inputs#I2`).
- Architecture `decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions`: `process_custom_widget_node` (`packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs`)
  and `draw_custom_widget` (`packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs`) are upstream functions; the addition goes into
  an escher function with one call in upstream's body.
- Design-system `decision/hit-test-stops-at-paint-clip` («a hit answers only what paint shows») bears on the clip
  option; layout-templates `decision/visible-region-through-clipping-boxes` on an element shot's crop.
- No playbook escalate pattern names this class by itself: it is no crossing (`rul-izni57qv` is not met). It is
  the founder's as a behaviour change for every document.

**Options, with their measured cost.** A is the fix; B and C are additions to A, each its own answer.
- **A — Fix the paint: the widget's `paint` is handed its content-box size × scale, and its scene is appended at
  the content origin inside the element's own transform (`M · T`).** Measured: the prototype is
  `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs` +9 −2 and `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` one line
  (`then_translate` → `pre_translate`, the form `draw_image` already uses at `render.rs:1516-1519`); the red
  readings above turn green; `stand_canvas_shot` and `custom_widget_layout` stay green. In the plan: one escher
  helper per upstream function (the fork-addition rule), a stand check of the three rows above in both layout
  modes, run red first. What it leaves: a widget that paints outside `(0, 0, width, height)` still shows past its
  content box (nothing clips it — B), and its pointer events stay in the border-box frame (C).
- **B — A, and clip the widget's scene to its content box**, as a replaced image is clipped
  (`with_replaced_content_clip`, `render.rs:1454-1478`). Cost: read, not built — one clip layer around the
  append, pushed always (a widget's scene has no known extent, where an image's overflow is computed), so one
  layer per painted widget per frame; the paint order around it (the viewport-wide blend layer, history
  `2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph`) stands. It changes what every widget can show: a widget drawing a
  shadow or a handle past its box today would lose it.
- **C — A, and give a widget its pointer events in the content-box frame.** Today `events/mod.rs:134` maps an event
  by `node.absolute_position(0.0, 0.0)`: the border-box origin, CSS px, through no transform (a sub-document's
  events are mapped the same way). After A alone, a widget with padding or a border paints from its content box
  and hears pointer coordinates from its border box, offset by its padding plus border. Cost: read, not built — the
  offset subtracted in the widget arm of `events/mod.rs` (blitz-dom, a file the pinned scope does not name, so the
  row read of the masters it reaches is re-run, about 12 minutes of batches at this take-up's measure); a transform
  stays unapplied to events either way. A pointer interaction on a widget is otherwise Epoch 4–5's ground
  (virtual nodes taking `click`; `drag`).
- **D — No engine change: leave the paint as upstream's**, and Circle Drawer's canvas (the later entry) keeps no
  padding, border or transform. Cost: none in code; the entry's first half is not done, v040-09's «placed at its
  content box» is unmet, and the defect stays reachable by any app that styles a widget.

**Dependences.** B and C each need A. F2 is independent of F1: canvas text lands where the scene lands, so under
A it lands inside the content box, under D at today's place. The stand checks this chunk adds pin the readings
of whichever options are taken; none moves a served task's reading (no served task holds a widget).

---

## Fork F2 — how a widget reaches the bundled fonts to draw canvas text (a public surface)

**What crosses.** No carrier moves; canvas text leaves only as pixels in a shot (settled — below). What is chosen
is a **public surface**: whether blitz-dom and upstream's `Widget` trait gain a way to hand a widget the document's
own font context, or the app shapes its text from its own context built from the same bundled bytes.

**The rule of ours it meets.**
- Test-plan / architecture, v030-14's verified acceptance (`cap:escher-0.3.0/v030-14`): «The bundled set is the
  document's own font context, the one every glyph run laid out in the document is shaped from, so canvas text
  (`GlyphRun`), a 0.4.0 reader, reads the same set.»
- Architecture `decision/stand-typography-dejavu-sans` and `decision/stand-uses-bundled-font`: every stand boot
  loads one font, the bundled DejaVu Sans, system fonts off; seven_guis' `DEJAVU_SANS` bytes compile on native.
- Architecture `decision/crate-internal-visibility` (internals `pub(crate)`): the document's `font_ctx` is
  `pub(crate)` today (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:264`); `decision/public-item-docs` and test-plan
  `decision/doc-leg-gates-public-doc-edits`: a new public item carries `///` and the doc leg joins the local gate.
- Security-plan `decision/no-agent-urls-through-font-path` and the stand's offline boot: no route from a widget,
  an app or an agent to a font fetch; `fonts-unavailable` keeps its meaning (`can_paint_text` reads the
  document's context).
- Security-plan `decision/harness-blitz-paint-custom-widget` / the Pinning rule: a new direct dependency of an
  escher crate is a reviewed pin; `parley` is already in `Cargo.lock`, so no package enters it.
- Test-plan history `2026-10-31-select-popup`: glyphs the engine paints differ under `blitz-paint/font-embolden`
  (macOS); a widget drawing its own glyph runs bypasses the engine's embolden and hinting (`packages/blitz-paint/src/text.rs:418-447`).

**Options, with their measured cost.**
- **A — The document's own font context, handed to the widget: a defaulted `Widget::fonts(&Arc<Mutex<FontContext>>)`
  method blitz-paint calls before each `paint`, and `BaseDocument::font_ctx()` made public (behind
  `custom-widget`).** Measured: the prototype is 14 added lines in 3 files (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` +6,
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs` +6,
  `packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs` +2); no implementor changes (the method is defaulted); the probe widget's text
  reads 557 dark pixels, both modes byte-equal. What it is: a new public method on upstream's trait and a new
  public accessor on `BaseDocument` (an upstream divergence, flagged upstreamable), and a **shared, mutable
  handle** to the document's font collection in app code: a widget could register fonts into the document and
  change how the page's own text lays out, and it locks the document's font mutex during paint. It meets v030-14's
  wording as written: canvas text shaped from the very context the document's text is.
- **B — The app's own font context from the same bundled bytes** (`build_single_font_ctx(seven_guis::DEJAVU_SANS)`,
  already public): no engine change, no new public item. Measured: the probe widget's text reads 557 dark pixels,
  byte-equal to A's on the stand. Cost: `parley` (and `anyrender`/`peniko`, if the stand's widget names them) as
  direct dependencies of seven_guis for the later Circle Drawer widget, and `parley` as a blitz-tests
  dev-dependency for this chunk's check — all already in `Cargo.lock`, a dependency-list move with no package; a
  second decoded copy of the font in memory per context. What it is: the same pixels on the stand only because the
  stand's document holds exactly that one font; off the stand (system fonts on, an `@font-face`) canvas text and
  page text can differ, and v030-14's «the document's own font context» sentence would read as not met by canvas
  text — a matrix-note or a re-wording the wrap records.
- **C — An engine text painter for widgets: blitz-dom/blitz-paint shape and paint a widget's text for it**
  (a new public API taking text, a size, a family and a colour, drawing through the engine's own glyph path, so
  canvas text takes the engine's embolden and hinting on every build). Cost: read, not built — a new public
  surface larger than A's (a text API and its types), the select list's paint-time text layout the only precedent
  (architecture `decision/paint-to-paint-scene` except); it is what «canvas text reads exactly like page text» on
  a `font-embolden` build would need.
- **D — No canvas text in this chunk:** text moves to «Circle Drawer on a canvas», which would take this fork. Cost:
  none now; the entry's second half is not done.

**Dependences.** Independent of F1 (above). Under A or B a widget's glyphs bypass the engine's embolden and hinting,
so a canvas-text pixel check is read on the `embolden` build as well, a pixel it moves pinned as a stated band
(test-plan `decision/expected-value-pinned-as-literal`'s except); under C they take the engine's. A and C each add
a public item, so the doc leg joins the local gate. B is the only option that leaves blitz-dom's public API as it is.

---

## Not a fork — settled by a standing record (named so the founder sees it)

- **Canvas text leaving as pixels in a shot.** The previous chunk's F1 (its `evidence/founder-forks.md`, lines
  79-80) stated: «The next entry, «Canvas placement and text», adds canvas text from the bundled fonts: under A
  that text crosses as pixels too, so A ratifies text the app draws into a canvas as well, not shapes alone.» The
  founder answered A, «Ратифицировать для всех каналов (Recommended)», recorded as architecture
  `decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels` and security-plan `decision/canvas-content-crosses-as-shot-pixels`. Canvas
  text adds no carrier, field or class beyond that ruling; nothing of it reaches a kept check (a shot is kept
  without pixels), the snapshot, a lint finding or a log.
- **A bundled font or asset entering the tree.** None on any option: A, B and C shape from the stand's existing
  `examples/seven_guis/assets/DejaVuSans.woff2` (`seven_guis::DEJAVU_SANS`), as the probe did.
- **Capability v040-09.** Not claimable by this chunk on any answer: its acceptance needs Circle Drawer on a canvas
  and the cross-host measurement, which «Circle Drawer on a canvas» and «Canvas shot across hosts» own; it stays
  pooled with a dated note.

A widget's paint size is its content box × scale: the border box less left/right and top/bottom border and padding, floored at 0. `process_custom_widget_node` calls it once, in place of upstream's two `final_layout().size` lines. Its one caller remains `build_custom_widget_scenes`.
  - `ElementCx::draw_custom_widget` (`packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` 1538). The scene is appended at `self.transform.pre_translate(content origin)` (`M · T`) in place of `then_translate` (`T · M`), and it stays unclipped. Its one caller remains `render_element`.
  - `blitz_dom::events` private `custom_widget_content_origin(node: &crate::Node, pos: Point<f32>) -> Point<f32>` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs` 33-43, behind `custom-widget`). It returns `pos` plus the node's `border.left + padding.left` and `border.top + padding.top`, in CSS px, untransformed. `handle_dom_event` calls it once, before the widget arm (185-186), and the arm passes the result to `map_dom_event_to_ui_event` in place of `pos` (196). The sub-document arm is unchanged.
  - `Widget::fonts(&mut self, fonts: &Arc<Mutex<parley::FontContext>>)` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs` 125-129). A new defaulted public trait method: the widget is handed the document's own font context before each paint, and the default ignores it. No implementor changed: `RedFill`, both `DemoWidget`s and `FpsWidget` keep the default.
  - `BaseDocument::font_ctx(&self) -> Arc<Mutex<parley::FontContext>>` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` 1413-1418, public, behind `custom-widget`): a clone of the document's shared font context.

This is the second instance of residual `res-evkq636g`, after the `url` move; no new residual is opened.
  - No manifest line and no `deny.toml` line changed. Gate 9 read `git diff --numstat d43bc0e7f… -- Cargo.lock` as `3+2`.

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - blitz-tests gains three integration-test targets, one file each: `stand_canvas_placement`, `stand_canvas_pointer_frame` and `stand_canvas_text`.
  - The `stand_*.rs` files under `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` move 66 → 69. Basis: `git ls-files 'tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs'` reads 66 at HEAD, and `ls tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs` reads 69 on the work tree.

Carried: **Symbols / APIs** (`custom_widget_content_origin`).
  - architecture §Standard Contracts: the `widget-trait` contract, plus a `BaseDocument · font_ctx` contract. Carried: **Symbols / APIs** (`Widget::fonts`, `BaseDocument::font_ctx`).

Carried: **Dependencies**. The audit reads `advisories ok, licenses ok` with `deny.toml` unchanged.
  - test-plan §2 Test Strategy: the three checks as witnesses. Carried: **Coverage of new surfaces**.

data.why: Ratified; answers upstream issue 1578, a direct engine change flagged upstreamable

**Why:** Recorded as a reviewed pin on the operator's wrap directive, delegate the operator, 2026-11-23 (the founder away); a master row of it read as an inventory the lockfile holds, so none was landed. The syn edges kept at 3.0.6 rest on the operator's word at the P4 stop.

The select model, a direct engine change for every document, remote pages included (flagged upstreamable, no upstream pull request open): a `select`'s choice, or a `multiple` select's chosen set, is held as its options' `CHECKED` element state, so `:checked` matches the chosen option, and an option created with a `selected` attribute is seeded `CHECKED`; its rules sit in the crate-private `node::select` (no public type), cited to the WHATWG `select` element — a select's options are its `option` children and its `optgroup` children's, in tree order, an option's disabled reading the one rule `option_disabled`, its own attribute or its group's, an option's label its non-empty `label` attribute else its stripped and collapsed text, its value its `value` attribute when present else the text, and a single-choice select is settled by HTML's selectedness setting algorithm (the last chosen option, else the first option not disabled); the mutator records every select whose children an entry point touches, every select entering the document and the select of a `multiple` write or removal (`record_select_of_multiple_write`), so a removal settles its set to one option, a `selected` write sets that option chosen and, on a single-choice select, its select's other options not, a `multiple` select's others left alone, a cleared one sets it not chosen, and `flush` settles every recorded select, firing no event; a focused drop-down, a single select of display size 1, its list closed, that is no disabled form control takes a pressed `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` to the next / previous enabled option and `Home` / `End` to the first / last (with none chosen `ArrowDown` reads as `Home` and `ArrowUp` as `End`), and a character pressed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead — the first enabled option whose label starts with the buffered text, in lower case, the buffer (`select_typeahead`) starting afresh for another select or once the document's clock has moved 1 s (`TYPEAHEAD_TIMEOUT`) — Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, opening its list, every other key doing nothing and a released Space doing nothing more; a single select whose `size` parses above 1 is an in-flow list box (display size 1 keeping the drop-down): it opens no list, arrows, Home, End and typeahead choose and scroll the row into view, a row click chooses that row alone whatever modifier, and nothing need be chosen; a focused `multiple` select takes its keys through `press_multiple_select_key`: `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp`, `Home` and `End` alone choose that row alone, with Shift span from the anchor, and with Ctrl or Meta move the current row and change nothing, a Space flips the current row with no typed text standing and joins the text otherwise, a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta chooses its match alone, and disabled rows are never chosen; a click on a select clears the typeahead and the text selection and focuses it, and on a drop-down, a single select of display size 1, opens its list or closes one standing, a disabled select neither focusing nor acting; on a `multiple` select's row `click_select_row`, behind an `option` arm of `handle_click`, stops at a disabled select, focuses the select and clears the typeahead and the text selection, a plain click choosing the row alone, Ctrl or Meta flipping it, Shift spanning, Shift with no cursor yet spanning from the last chosen row, and a disabled row changing nothing; every choice that changes the chosen option or a `multiple` select's chosen set goes through `apply_select_choice`, which takes the chosen set — the `CHECKED` write, the changed set, `input` then `change`, each carrying `select_value`, and a redraw — and a single select's choice of its chosen option fires nothing; the public read-only `BaseDocument::select_value(&self, select: NodeId) -> Option<String>` is HTML's `select.value` — the chosen option's value, a `multiple` select's first chosen option in tree order (`None` with none chosen or for a node that is no select), its callers dioxus-native-dom's snapshot `value` and `apply_select_choice` — beside the public read-only `select_values(&self, select: NodeId) -> Vec<String>` (the chosen set) and `select_of(&self, node: NodeId) -> Option<NodeId>` (an option's or group's select) and `is_list_box` (true for a select with `multiple` or a display size above 1, false for a stale or non-select id) and the public `clear_select_typeahead(&mut self)`, its one non-test caller escher-driver's `focus_select`; an open list's API on `BaseDocument` — public read-only `open_select`, `select_list_bounds`, `select_list_view` and `select_row_layout`, public `close_select_list` (its callers keyboard, pointer, reconcile and the driver's `focus_select`), the rest crate-private or private, the list's state in the crate-private `node::select_list` but for two public read types re-exported from the crate root, `SelectListView`, the list's colours its associated constants, and `SelectListRow`; form submission sends every chosen option that is not disabled, by its value; the accessibility builder keeps an option whose parent is a `select`, or an `optgroup` under one, although it computes `display: none` (`hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still exclude it); and the user-agent stylesheet gives `select` the border, padding and background of `input, textarea`, `display: inline-block`, and shows a single-choice select's chosen option by `select:not([multiple]) > option:checked { display: inline; }`, so a single-choice select lays out as a box holding its chosen option; the default sheet lays out `optgroup` and `multiple` rows — under a single select a group `display: contents` and its chosen option `display: inline`, under a `multiple` select rows and groups `display: block` — and holds the engine-default chosen-row pair `background-color: #c8c8c8; color: #000000` for a `multiple` select's rows (12.56:1, hardcoded since the engine holds no tokens), a single list box's chosen row taking the same pair as presentational hints. Its limits: an option of a closed drop-down, a single select of display size 1, under a group too, is not clicked (a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`), a single select of display size 1 stays a drop-down — a `multiple` select's `size`, or a single select's above 1, hints a `height` of `size` × 1.2em through `size_rows`, capped at 65534, `0` or a bad value no hint, with `select[multiple][size] { overflow-y: auto; }` and `line-height: 1.2` on its rows in the default sheet, and a key brings the current row into view only where the select carries a valid `size` — and Ctrl+A is not modelled; a `multiple` select and an `optgroup`'s options are modelled in the keys, pointer, form, tree, sheet, snapshot and bridge. The select list stands beside the select model, a direct engine change for every document, remote pages included, ratified, its merge surface the sixteen files of `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/evidence/merge-surface.md`, a line owned by Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration: a drop-down, a single select of display size 1, opens a list the engine paints over the page by a click, by Enter, or by a Space with no typed text standing, a bound label's click focusing the select and opening nothing; the list shows at most `MAX_ROWS` (20) rows, opens where its rows fit and else on the side with more room, is at least its select's width and at most the viewport's, and a select with no row to show opens nothing; `SelectList.fresh` holds a just-opened list against a `:focus` rule's restyle; it closes with no event on Escape, a second click on the select, a press outside, a wheel outside the list and a page scroll or move of the select's box, and removal, `disabled`, `hidden` or `inert` on the select closes it too; Tab chooses the current row and closes before focus moves, in either direction; Enter, Space and a click on a row choose through `apply_select_choice`, a disabled row changing nothing and leaving the list open; the move keys shift the highlight over enabled rows and choose nothing; a wheel over the list scrolls the list alone and a wheel elsewhere closes it and then scrolls. Its limit: the thumb is painted and not draggable; the lint reads an open list's highlighted row at its painted pair, the engine's highlight colours, its rows take one height, the tallest row's line with the select's own one-line height as the floor, so a row with a larger authored font is painted whole, and while a single select's list stands open with a current option the tree names that option as the select's active descendant, and none while closed, the tree's focus staying on the select and a page's `aria-activedescendant` never read.

- Custom widgets are pre-painted into Scenes keyed by document and node id; a widget's paint size is its content box times the scale (the border box less border and padding, floored at 0) and its scene is appended at the content origin inside the element's transform, unclipped (ratified, answering upstream issue 1578, a direct engine change flagged upstreamable; `stand_canvas_placement`).

An `optgroup` is read by a closed element-name match, `options` walking a select's `option` children and its `optgroup` children's in tree order, a group taking `Role::Group` and its non-empty `label` its name in the tree, inside the ratified name crossing, and a header painted in an open list, leaving also as pixels in a `screenshot`, a boundary widening ratified — an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified as to the list through a group and as to the `label` as a name. Behind the `custom-widget` feature, `ElementData::set_custom_widget` replays each existing attribute, parsed page content included, to `Widget::attribute_changed` with no old value, so a widget receives them at set-up and not only on a later change, the value's check staying the widget's own — an engine change for every document behind the feature, ratified. Behind the same feature a custom widget is handed the document's own shared, mutable font context before each paint, the base document exposing it publicly, so app widget code holds a live handle to the engine's font context — no input crosses, the default ignores it, ratified.

title: a `url` update re-resolves two `syn` edges into a lock that does not build: the committed lock holds `url` 2.5.9 and `fo
body: a `url` update re-resolves two `syn` edges into a lock that does not build: the committed lock holds `url` 2.5.9 and `form_urlencoded` 1.2.3 with the `syn` edges of `bindgen` 0.73.2 and `cssparser-macros` 0.7.1 kept at 3.0.6 by edit (the operator's ruling «Keep syn edges (Recommended)» at implement), a state `cargo update -p url` does not produce; on the base lock `cargo update -p url` — alone, `--precise 2.5.9`, or beside `-p form_urlencoded` — moves both edges to `syn` 2.0.119, and `bindgen` 0.73.2, whose `prettyplease` 0.3.0 stays on `syn` 3.0.6, then fails to compile (E0277, `syn::file::File: syn::parse_quote::ParseQuote`); `cargo update -p log` and `-p regex` move no `syn` edge, and a whole `cargo update` moves every `syn 3` edge to 3.0.10 (its build unmeasured). Reproduce: `cargo update -p url --precise 2.5.9 && git diff -U0 Cargo.lock` (two `- "syn 3.0.6", + "syn 2.0.119",` pairs), then `cargo build --workspace --locked`. Any later url update, an upstream sync's lock take included, re-breaks the build until `bindgen` and `prettyplease` agree on `syn`; held as a residual on the operator's wrap directive (chunks/2026-11-22-epoch-2-corrective/inputs/I6-epoch2-corrective-wrap-directive-2026-11-22.md.txt point 3; chunks/2026-11-22-epoch-2-corrective/inputs/I5-relay-1.md.txt; the measurement chunks/2026-11-22-epoch-2-corrective/evidence/url-lock-move.diff). Second instance at 2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text: `cargo update -p cookie --precise 0.18.3`, the patch for RUSTSEC-2026-0594, moved the same two edges to `syn` 2.0.119, so `cookie` 0.18.3 was taken by editing its `version` and `checksum` lines alone and the edges stay at 3.0.6 (the operator's word at that P4 stop, chunks/2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text/inputs/I10-relay-2.md.txt; the measurement chunks/2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text/evidence/cookie-lock-move.diff); a later lock-only bump of any crate whose `cargo update -p` re-resolves the pair is made the same way, and amended here, no new residual (the operator's wrap directive point 4, chunks/2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text/inputs/I11-canvas-placement-and-text-wrap-directive-2026-11-23.md.txt)
